title: ToList and multiple enumeration
sub: When to store the result, and when not to
cards/0/body: A query does not remember its result. Enumerate it twice and the whole chain runs twice: reading again, Where again, Select again. If the source is a database or a file, that is two trips to it.
cards/1/task: The query is enumerated twice: Count() and foreach. Make the source read at most 6 times in total.
cards/2/q: With ToList, why is the source read only once even though it is still enumerated twice?
cards/2/options/0: ToList ran the chain once and stored a list; Count() and foreach work on that list
cards/2/explain: Once materialized, you enumerate the list, not the query.
cards/3/task: Here ToList is unnecessary: because of it, Where runs for all six numbers. Get Where down to at most 4 calls.
cards/4/q: With ToList before Take, why did Where run 6 times?
cards/4/options/0: ToList needs every element, so Take can no longer stop the reading
cards/4/explain: ToList is a wall: everything before it runs to completion.
cards/5/body:
Materialize (ToList, ToArray) if the result is enumerated several times or the source is expensive.
Don't materialize if you enumerate once or a Take/First comes later — laziness saves work.

The IDE warns you: "Possible multiple enumeration".
cards/6/q: Where does the database query run a second time?
cards/6/explain: Any() ran the query, and foreach runs it again. If you need all the users, call ToList() right away.
cards/7/q: When should you call ToList()? Select all.
cards/7/options/0: The result is enumerated several times
cards/7/options/1: The source is a slow database or file, and you need the result later
cards/7/options/2: You need to freeze the data before the source changes
cards/7/explain: Before First(), ToList only forces reading everything.
